subject: Creating Composits/Formative Latent Variables with Ordinal Observed Variables

messages.author: afad425dd9c86301
messages.subject: Creating Composits/Formative Latent Variables with Ordinal Observed Variables
parts:
Hello everyone,

I'm try to build a run-of-the-mill path analysis model with the following four variables:
  1. Social status (a composite)
  2. National economic perceptions (latent variable)
  3. Personal economic perceptions (latent variable)
  4. Political party identification (binary, 1 = incumbent governing party, 0 = other party)
The syntax for the paths would be as follows:

national_econ ~ 1 + social_status
personal_econ ~ 1 + social_status
partyid ~ social_status + national_econ + personal_econ

national_econ ~~ personal_econ

However, I can't get the social status composite to work. The variables that make it up -- sector of employment, education, household income, and housing tenure -- are all categorical variables. Is it possible to build composite variables in lavaan using categorical indicators? If so, could anyone give me some advice on how to do it?

Thanks in advance,

Jack

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Creating Composits/Formative Latent Variables with Ordinal Observed Variables
parts: lavaan is a package for factor-based SEM. Composites are not factors, so your functionality would be limited, even if your variables were interval or ratio scaled. No, you cannot meaningfully add categorical variables together. You could transform your categorical variables into dichotomous dummy variables and use those collectively to represent the original categorical variables. You could use the "blcok variable" method of Heise (see attached) to capture the joint effects of the transformed categorical predictors, and use that as the effect of the "composite" you want to create.
